evals.prompt: I have an approved parent plan for adding OAuth login to our web app. Break it down into detailed implementation subplans I can hand off for execution.
assertions: No single subplan is given more than 7 tasks (work is split into subplans of roughly 5-7 tasks each)
Execution ordering (parallel vs sequential) is decided by whether subplans touch overlapping files/packages: non-overlapping ones may run in parallel, overlapping ones are sequenced

evals.prompt: Before we plan this data-layer refactor, help me settle the open design decisions. There are several unresolved trade-offs (naming, where the migration logic lives, and how much of the old contract to keep).
assertions: Presents only ONE decision at a time and stops for the answer, rather than listing or batching all the decisions in one response
The decision is presented as prose with an explicit recommended option (not a neutral multiple-choice list and not a forced-option question widget)

evals.prompt: Resume the implementation work on my authentication plan, which has several subplans.
assertions: Establishes a baseline by running validation (typecheck / lint / build / tests) before making code changes
Works on a single plan/subplan and stops when it is complete instead of automatically continuing to the next subplan

evals.prompt: Create a high-level plan for adding rate limiting to our API, based on the research we just did.
assertions: The plan includes a non-empty skills_to_consult list naming applicable coding-guideline skills for implementers
It stops at the high-level/parent plan and does NOT write out detailed implementation subplans in the same pass

evals.prompt: Run discovery on the dispatch-delay problem. We use a hosted tracker, do not want user stories by default, and may lose this agent session before formulation.
assertions: Produces a canonical Discovery result with observations, assumptions, unknowns, and affected context without requiring user-story or Gherkin form
Publishes through the selected provider and returns an opaque native reference that can be resolved after context loss

evals.prompt: Research whether our support assistant can process EU customer transcripts. Separate evidence from synthesis, state confidence, and account for privacy and regulated applicability.
assertions: Separates cited evidence and provenance from synthesized findings, limitations, uncertainty, and open questions
Records applicable data-access, external-research, privacy, and regulated constraints

evals.prompt: Critique solution design design:payments-v3 at revision sha256:91af, then let our architecture owner decide whether to accept it.
assertions: Critique runs in fresh independent context and remains separate from revision and acceptance
Acceptance binds to the exact native revision and preserves the human authority reference rather than allowing the model to fabricate authority

evals.prompt: Create a planning result from research result:782 and decision R-18. The result provider is our task database, not files or Git.
assertions: Consumes the opaque native input references by asking the selected providers to resolve them rather than parsing their shapes
Publishes a provider-native Planning result and does not silently fall back to a local plan file or require Git
